title: Mantis shrimp red-sensitive pigments act as reversible light switches
content: Researchers from the University of Liège and Humboldt University in Berlin have, for the first time, examined mantis shrimp visual pigments individually. Their analysis identified several red‑sensitive pigments—rare among animals—in a system that contains roughly 30 pigments compared with the three found in humans. The results, detailed in Science Advances, suggest these pigments function as reversible light switches and could be leveraged for optogenetic applications.
summary: Researchers from ULiège and Humboldt University in Berlin analyzed mantis shrimp visual pigments individually and found that some red‑sensitive pigments act as reversible light switches. The study, published in Science Advances, notes that these pigments detect red light rarely perceived by other animals and could be useful for optogenetics.
author: Phys.org

title: FAST telescope finds hydrogen cloud with 500,000 solar masses, possible dark galaxy
content:
Astronomers using China’s FAST radio telescope have discovered a compact cloud of hydrogen with no visible stars or galaxy around it.  

The object, containing nearly 500,000 times the sun’s mass in neutral hydrogen, is described as one of the strongest isolated “dark galaxy” candidates. The discovery was detailed in a paper posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 24.
summary: Astronomers using China's FAST radio telescope discovered a compact cloud of hydrogen with no visible stars or galaxy around it. The cloud, containing nearly 500,000 times the sun's mass in neutral hydrogen, is a strong candidate for an isolated dark galaxy, and the discovery paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 24.
author: Phys.org

title: James Webb finds three-state orderly weather on turbulent world 20 ly away
content:
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has revealed that a turbulent world 20 light‑years away exhibits an orderly weather system.  

The system cycles through three recurring atmospheric states driven by temperature shifts and cloud movements, a breakthrough that provides scientists a new tool to study weather patterns on distant planets and the atmospheric conditions that shape them.
summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope revealed that a turbulent world 20 light‑years away has a surprisingly orderly weather system. The system shows three recurring atmospheric states driven by temperature changes and shifting clouds, giving scientists a new tool for studying distant worlds’ weather patterns.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists link dysfunctional brain cells to abnormal myelin and cognitive decline
content:
Scientists have identified that certain protective brain cells may actually drive age‑related cognitive decline. When these cells malfunction, they generate excess myelin, which interferes with nerve fiber integrity.  

The disruption is linked to worsening memory and thinking abilities in older individuals.
summary: Scientists have uncovered a cause of age‑related cognitive decline involving brain cells previously thought to be entirely beneficial. When these cells become dysfunctional they can produce abnormal amounts of myelin, disrupting nerve fibers and potentially contributing to worsening memory and thinking skills.
author: Science Daily

title: Stanford scientists unveil microscope that images living cells in real time without labels
content:
Stanford scientists have developed a revolutionary microscope that reveals the hidden inner workings of living cells in real time, without the fluorescent labels that can interfere with observations.  

The breakthrough could provide new insights into cancer, infectious diseases and how drugs interact with cells.
summary: Stanford scientists have developed a revolutionary microscope that reveals the hidden inner workings of living cells in real time without fluorescent labels. The breakthrough could provide new insights into cancer, infectious diseases, and how drugs interact with cells.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists discover European nightjar trades speed for agility, generates upward thrust
content:
Scientists have uncovered an unexpected trade‑off in the wings of the European nightjar, a bird that migrates thousands of kilometres.  

The species sacrifices high‑speed flight efficiency to hunt insects with remarkable agility and generates thrust on the upward wingbeat, a technique that could inspire new flying technologies.
summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected trade‑off in the wings of the European nightjar, which migrates thousands of kilometers but sacrifices high‑speed flight efficiency to hunt insects with remarkable agility. The bird also generates thrust on the upward wingbeat, a technique that could inspire new flying technologies.
author: Science Daily

title: SpaceX delivers strange cargo including brain models and retinal tech to ISS
content:
SpaceX delivered a notably unconventional payload to the International Space Station, according to the latest shipment report.  

The cargo includes tiny brain models, three‑dimensional heart tissue and equipment for manufacturing artificial retinas in microgravity, experiments that scientists say could lead to new treatments for severe brain disorders, restore vision and enable testing of future medicines.  

Also aboard are materials intended to produce unusual glass in near weightlessness and the station’s final upgraded solar arrays.
summary: SpaceX delivered a cargo shipment to the International Space Station that includes tiny brain models, 3D heart tissue, and technology for making artificial retinas in space. The shipment also contains materials for creating unusual glass in near weightlessness and the station’s final upgraded solar arrays.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope delivers image quality about 30% better than expected
content: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has outperformed its design specifications after engineers made minute adjustments to its optics. By shifting a mirror by an amount equivalent to one‑sixteenth the width of a human hair, the team aligned the telescope’s instruments with near‑perfect precision. The correction boosted the Wide Field Instrument’s image quality to nearly 30 % better than originally predicted, enhancing the telescope’s capability for exceptionally sharp cosmic surveys.
summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope exceeded expectations after engineers moved a mirror by one‑sixteenth the width of a human hair to improve alignment. Roman’s Wide Field Instrument now achieves image quality nearly 30% better than predicted, enabling sharper cosmic surveys.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA discovers dozens of hidden fires beneath Amazon rainforest
content:
NASA researchers have uncovered dozens of previously undetected fires burning beneath the Amazon rainforest, suggesting the damage may be more extensive than satellite records indicate.

Scientists say El Niño is driving a dangerous cascade of wildfires across the tropics, with the Amazon now seeing widespread burning and warnings that the worst could still be ahead.
summary: El Niño is fueling a dangerous cascade of wildfires across the tropics, with the Amazon rainforest now experiencing widespread burning. NASA researchers are uncovering dozens of previously undetected fires, suggesting the destruction could be more extensive than satellite records show.
author: Science Daily

title: SpaceX Falcon 9 launch creates jellyfish-shaped glow over eastern US
content: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launched early morning, creating a jellyfish‑shaped glow across the eastern United States as sunlight illuminated its exhaust. The NASA mission delivered equipment and scientific experiments to the International Space Station, including research aimed at advancing treatments for blindness, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and other diseases.
summary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launched early in the morning, producing a jellyfish-shaped glow across the eastern United States as sunlight illuminated its exhaust. The mission delivered equipment and scientific experiments to the International Space Station, including research aimed at advancing treatments for blindness, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and other diseases.
author: Science Daily

title: Pete Hegseth’s livestream execution plan condemned, but experts say many will watch
content:
US defence secretary Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan has drawn condemnation from human rights groups and politicians across the spectrum.  

Coltan Scrivner, an author and psychologist at Arizona State University, says that despite the backlash, large numbers are likely to watch, explaining the attraction to dark and disturbing content.  

Madeleine Finlay tells Ian Sample that consuming such material can harm observers’ mental health.
summary: US defence secretary Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan has incurred condemnation from human rights groups and politicians on all sides. But according to Coltan Scrivner, an author and psychologist at Arizona State University and expert on morbid curiosity, people are still likely to watch in large numbers.
author: Guardian Science

title: Creator builds Zelda timeline ahead of Ocarina of Time remake release
content: I made this ahead of the Ocarina of Time remake which comes out in 17 days. I remember the feeling of playing it as a kid but I hadn’t kept up with the story so I built a timeline to catch up before the Door of Time reopens. Nintendo’s own timeline is the authority here (Hyrule Historia and their chronicle page). The fun part was rethinking how to visualize it. It branches at the end of Ocarina into three eras depending on whether Link wins or loses, so each era is its own thread on the cloth. The threads meet again much later with Breath of the Wild. I had a lot of help from Claude. I’d often thought about building things like this but never found the time between the day job and the rest of life. Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50140769 Points: 29 # Comments: 6
summary: A creator made a visual Zelda timeline to catch up before the Ocarina of Time remake, which arrives in 17 days. The timeline follows Nintendo’s official chronology, showing the post‑Ocarina branches into three eras that later converge in Breath of the Wild.
author: Hacker News

title: Lenovo Legion Go S handheld with SteamOS discounted to $999.99 at Best Buy
content:
Lenovo’s Legion Go S handheld, now running SteamOS, is being sold at a discounted price of $999.99 at Best Buy, down from its listed $1,579.99. The device pairs the Ryzen Z1 Extreme processor with 32 GB of RAM and a 1 TB solid‑state drive, and it features an eight‑inch IPS panel that delivers 1080p resolution at up to 120 Hz—specifications that surpass the $789 Steam Deck OLED’s 800p screen and 90 Hz refresh rate.

The Go S also includes two‑stage triggers and a design aimed at comfort, positioning it as a solid alternative to the Deck. While it offers more power than the Steam Deck, it trails the $1,299.99 Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20, which uses a Ryzen Z2 Extreme chip and an OLED display.

The model originally launched with Windows 11 and a Ryzen Z2 Go processor, but the discounted configuration swaps in the faster Z1 Extreme and SteamOS for a better handheld experience. For further performance details, readers can refer to Sean Hollister’s review and benchmarks of the Go S configurations.
summary: Lenovo Legion Go S handheld with SteamOS discounted to $999.99 at Best Buy.
author: The Verge

title: Looters raid and vandalise shops across France during massive protests
content: Looters on Saturday took advantage of massive protests across France, raiding and vandalising a range of shops and businesses, from bakeries and supermarkets to tech stores. The attacks unfolded while hundreds of thousands of people were on the streets protesting higher living costs and other grievances.
summary: Looters on Saturday raided and vandalised a range of shops and businesses across France, from bakeries and supermarkets to tech stores. The attacks took place while hundreds of thousands of people were on the streets protesting higher living costs and other grievances.
author: France 24

title: Atlanta ‘No Kings’ rally urges vote, denounces Trump ahead of midterms
content: “No Kings, Vote Now” was the theme of a rally in Atlanta on Saturday, part of a series of events across the US. Demonstrators denounced President Donald Trump’s policies, and organizers said the gathering aimed to boost turnout for the November 3 midterm elections and protect American democracy.
summary: The “No Kings, Vote Now” rally was held in Atlanta on Saturday as part of a series of events across the United States. Demonstrators criticized President Donald Trump’s policies and organizers said the rally aimed to boost turnout for the November 3 midterm elections and protect American democracy.
author: France 24

title: Rubio says Trump’s 60‑day pause on Russia sanctions to be analyzed globally
content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump will pause waiving sanctions and tariffs on Russia for 60 days and will analyze the global impact of the sanctions during that pause.  

The decision has drawn bipartisan criticism and sparked concerns in Ukraine that Washington may further ease restrictions on Moscow.
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sanctions and tariffs on Russia will last 60 days. He noted the move has drawn bipartisan criticism and raised concerns in Ukraine that Washington could further ease restrictions on Moscow.
author: France 24

title: Macron to address nation at 8 pm after protests with over 1,800 arrests
content: French President Emmanuel Macron will address the nation at 8pm this evening following Saturday's demonstrations which saw more than 1,800 people arrested alongside peaceful marches. US President Donald Trump weighed in on the events, saying "France is burning" via his social media platform Truth Social. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron will address the nation at 8 pm following Saturday's demonstrations that led to more than 1,800 arrests and included peaceful marches. US President Donald Trump said “France is burning” on his Truth Social platform.
author: France 24

title: India releases Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke from police custody
content:
Indian police released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke from detention on Saturday after he had been held ahead of a rally demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner.  

Two other CJP leaders remain in custody, having been arrested while demonstrating at a protest site that police had declared off‑limits.
summary: Indian police released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke from detention on Saturday. Two other CJP leaders remain in custody after being arrested while demonstrating at a police‑restricted protest site.
author: France 24

title: India’s youth‑led Cockroach movement faces crackdown, leaders jailed, protest site closed
content:
A fresh wave of demonstrations by India’s youth‑led Cockroach movement has encountered a harsh crackdown from Narendra Modi’s government, which also ordered the closure of a historic protest site in Delhi.  

Two movement leaders were detained for five days after authorities said they breached suppression measures. The protests, originally sparked by frustration over education and unemployment, have shifted to demand voting‑rights protections. Modi’s government rejects accusations that it aims to disenfranchise millions of voters, while the United Nations and Amnesty International have condemned the treatment of demonstrators, warning that India may be sliding toward autocracy. Lucy Hough interviews South Asia correspondent Hannah Ellis‑Petersen on the issue.
summary: A fresh wave of protests by India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has been met with a brutal crackdown by Narendra Modi’s government and the closure of a historic protest site in Delhi. Two of the movement’s leaders have been imprisoned for five days for violating suppression measures.
author: Guardian World

title: Roof collapse at al-Khair school in Peshawar kills at least 34 children and a teacher
content:
A roof collapse at the privately run al‑Khair school in Peshawar killed at least 34 schoolchildren and a female teacher during morning classes.

Rescue workers spent hours pulling children from the rubble, while three pupils remain in critical condition. Panicked parents and relatives thronged the site searching for loved ones.
summary: At least 34 schoolchildren and a female teacher died when the roof of the privately run al‑Khair school collapsed during morning classes in the northern Pakistani city of Peshawar. Three additional pupils are in critical condition as rescue workers continue searching for survivors.
author: Guardian World

title: Cockroach Janta party leader Abhijeet Dipke arrested in Delhi ahead of protest
content: The leader of the Cockroach Janta Party youth movement, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained by police on Friday and subsequently formally arrested as authorities intensified a crackdown on fresh anti‑government protests in Delhi. Dipke had called for a Friday‑evening demonstration in central Delhi, urging supporters to gather and hold up the Indian flag. Police detained him shortly before the planned rally, citing the broader effort to suppress the newly organized protests.
summary: Abhijeet Dipke, leader of the Cockroach Janta party youth movement, was detained by police on Friday in Delhi. He was later formally arrested as authorities cracked down on fresh anti‑government protests before a planned evening demonstration he had called.
author: Guardian World

title: Reviewers Praise Guardian’s NAZA Documentary on Gaza Civilian Mass Killing
content: Film interviewing military insiders about mass killing of civilians in Gaza wins widespread praise around the world Critics around the world have hailed the award-winning documentary NAZA as a “brilliant and harrowing” film that is “impossible to ignore”. NAZA, which is produced by the Guardian and details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, was released in UK cinemas this week and will be shown in more than 50 countries. As well as its global cinema releases, NAZA will be available free on the Guardian’s website from late November.
summary: Reviewers Praise Guardian’s NAZA Documentary on Gaza Civilian Mass Killing.
author: Guardian World

title: Israeli settlers attack olive harvesters and Washington Post photographer in West Bank
content:
Israeli settlers launched coordinated attacks on Palestinians harvesting olives in the occupied West Bank on Friday, targeting farmers and Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine as part of a yearly effort to disrupt the olive harvest.  

Masked settlers wielding clubs, rocks and other weapons hurled projectiles at the harvesters, beat the journalist and set fire to cars and trees. Palestinian authorities said the assaults occurred in eight villages and left at least 20 people injured.
summary: Masked Israeli settlers wielding clubs, rocks and other weapons attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in West Bank towns, burning cars and trees and beating Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine. Palestinian authorities said the coordinated attacks occurred in eight villages and injured at least 20 people.
author: Guardian World

title: Gaza war separates Wijdan Abu Matar from injured husband after 17 Oct strike
content:
Wijdan Abu Matar, 43, was compelled to leave Gaza in November 2023 with her eight children for medical treatment, leaving her injured husband, Hatem, behind. The family resided in the Nuseirat refugee camp when the conflict began following the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack on Israel. On 17 October, an Israeli strike targeted the al-Muhandseen tower near their home, injuring Wijdan and every other member of the family.

This incident exemplifies how the war has scattered families and prevented couples from reuniting or marrying. Wijdan’s separation from her husband highlights the broader struggle of individuals unable to carry the burden of displacement and injury alone amidst the ongoing crisis.
summary: Gaza war separates Wijdan Abu Matar from injured husband after 17 Oct strike.
author: Guardian World

title: UAE to resume payments to Yemeni forces as Saudi Arabia provides air cover
content:
The United Arab Emirates has agreed to re‑enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to certain government forces fighting the Iran‑aligned Houthi fighters in the south, according to Yemeni sources. In exchange, Saudi Arabia will provide air cover for the anti‑Houthi forces.

The arrangement marks the first concrete sign that the long‑standing rift between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over Yemen’s future is beginning to heal, driven by recent Houthi advances that have alarmed Gulf state rulers. Both Gulf nations are coordinating their support as the Houthi gains intensify, signaling a renewed joint effort to bolster the Yemeni government side against the rebel group.
summary: The United Arab Emirates has agreed to re‑enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to some government forces fighting Iran‑aligned Houthis in the south. Saudi Arabia will provide air cover for those anti‑Houthi forces, marking a new cooperation between the two Gulf states.
author: Guardian World

title: French government in crisis talks after violent unrest burns buildings, 2000 arrested
content:
The French government entered crisis talks on Sunday after a day of unrest described as one of the most violent in years, during which public buildings were set ablaze, hundreds of shops were destroyed and looted, and more than 2,000 people were arrested across the country.  

Ministers, officials and police are under pressure as politicians from both the left and right have called for the resignation of interior minister Laurent Nuñez, saying the administration was caught by surprise by the scale of the violence that saw state buildings stormed and torched, bus stops smashed, roads barricaded and shops broken into and destroyed.
summary: French government in crisis talks after violent unrest burns buildings, 2000 arrested.
author: Guardian World

title: The X-Files' is officially returning as Hulu picks up Ryan Coogler's 'reimagining' of the sci-fi icon
content: The truth is once again out there, as Disney & Hulu confirmed today that they have picked up a new "The X-Files" show for a full season. Described as a "reimagining" of the classic series, the project comes from Ryan Coogler, the acclaimed writer and director of "Creed", "Black Panther", and "Sinners", and will star Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel. The show's premise will sound very familiar to fans of the original, as it centers on "two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents who form an unlikely bond when they are assigned to a long-shuttered division devoted to cases involving unexplained phenomena." "I've loved 'The X-Files' for a long time, so getting the chance to write and direct the pilot has meant a great deal to me," said Coogler. "What Chris Carter created is special, and we wanted to honor everything that made the original series connect with so many people while also finding our own way into that world." Coogler wrote, directed, and executive produced the pilot for this new show, which impressed executives over at Hulu enough to give the show the greenlight. He's certainly got the pedigree when it comes to "spooky", as "Sinners" was a modern horror masterpiece, winning the Best Original Screenplay Oscar at the 2025 Academy Awards. The X-Files is one of the greatest sci-fi shows of all time, and we can't wait to see what a modern take on the classic formula looks like. (Image credit: Getty Images (Gilbert Flores)) Alongside the leads, the cast will include Amy Madigan, Ben Foster, Devery Jacobs, Lochlyn Munro, Tantoo Cardinal, Joel D. Montgrand, Sofia Grace Clifton, and Hollywood legend Steve Buscemi (an inspired casting choice for any show, but especially here. He looks like a man who's seen the truth). Both Coogler and Hulu are being coy about how this new series will fit into the continuity of the original show. It's being described as a reimagining, but they've stopped short of calling it a reboot, which could leave the door open for Mulder and Scully to return in some capacity. The original creator of "The X-Files", Chris Carter, is also on board as an executive producer, which is great news for fans who are hoping this new incarnation keeps the spirit of the original alive. There is no confirmed release date yet, but Ryan Coogler's The X-Files project will launch exclusively on Hulu (US) & Disney+ (UK). Watch The X-Files on Hulu (US): Hulu with Ads: $11.99/month or $119.99/year Premium (No Ads): $18.99/month
summary: The X-Files' is officially returning as Hulu picks up Ryan Coogler's 'reimagining' of the sci-fi icon.
author: Space.com

title: ‘Testosterone to burn’: Kagiso Rabada plays down 2018 clash with Australia’s Steve Smith
content:
Kagiso Rabada says “There’s no hate,” as he prepares to return to St George’s Park, downplaying the heated 2018 clash with Australia’s Steve Smith that unfolded in Gqeberha six years ago. The South African fast‑bowler insists there is no lingering bad blood with the visitors ahead of the second Test.

Rabada has been declared fit after a hamstring tear and will face Australia in his first match since May. His comeback comes at a crucial stage, with the hosts fighting to stay alive after their 214‑run pumping in Durban last week.
summary: ‘Testosterone to burn’: Kagiso Rabada plays down 2018 clash with Australia’s Steve Smith.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts placed on IR after calf blood clot diagnosis
content:
Quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after the Philadelphia Eagles confirmed he had a blood clot in his calf.  

Hurts was first ruled out on Thursday for the Eagles’ upcoming game against Carolina after the team said he had been injured when he took a cleat to his calf during their game against the Los Angeles Rams on October 4.  

The Eagles said the blood clot requires Hurts to miss at least four games, and the Super Bowl MVP will be sidelined for the remainder of the season.
summary: Quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after the Philadelphia Eagles revealed he had a blood clot in his calf. He had been ruled out on Thursday and was originally injured when a cleat struck his calf during the October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Daniel Dubois stops Fabio Wardley in second round to retain WBO heavyweight title
content: Dubois underlines status as Britain’s leading heavyweight Wardley’s corner throw in the towel in second round Daniel Dubois overwhelmed Fabio Wardley in their WBO world title fight on Saturday night as he continued his quest to become the most authoritative heavyweight fighter on the planet with this crushing victory. This was the second time in five months that Dubois has defeated Wardley but, after their fight of the year contender in May, he unleashed a shockingly one-sided shellacking. After two minutes and 21 seconds of round two, Wardley was rescued from the bludgeoning fists of Dubois by the referee, just as the fluttering white towel of his trainer, Ben Davison, sailed over the ropes in surrender. Davison had been on the brink of throwing in the towel at the very end of the opening round but the bell sounded to end a disastrous first three minutes for Wardley. He was dropped heavily after just 17 seconds as Dubois landed a left cross followed by a pulverising right hand.
summary: Daniel Dubois stopped Fabio Wardley by referee intervention at 2:21 of the second round, retaining his WBO heavyweight title. Wardley’s corner threw in the towel after he was knocked down early in the round by a left cross and a right hand.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Air Force officer dies after falling from Alamodome rafters before UTSA-Navy game
content:
An Air Force officer died after falling from the rafters of the Alamodome during a pre‑game display for the University of Texas at San Antonio’s home football game against Navy on Saturday. The officer, whose name was not released, was participating in UTSA’s “Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans” night when he slipped while rappelling down from the stadium’s overhead structure.

He landed on the field and received immediate treatment before being placed on a stretcher and taken to a local hospital. He later succumbed to his injuries. Nellis Air Force Base identified the officer as a member of the 6th Combat Training Squadron, a unit that trains military personnel to rappel from helicopters. The incident occurred before the game began, prompting an abrupt end to the ceremonial display.
summary: Air Force officer dies after falling from Alamodome rafters before UTSA-Navy game.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wigan remain bottom of League One despite 1-0 win over Reading
content:
Wigan Athletic remain at the foot of League One even after a 1‑0 victory over Reading on Saturday, underscoring the gap between their current struggles and the club’s historic high point. The win did little to lift the Latics from the bottom of the third tier, a stark contrast to the euphoria of the 2013 FA Cup final when they famously defeated Manchester City.

Gary Caldwell, who captained the side in that triumph, is now manager and faces the task of turning the season around. Caldwell returned for a second spell after a stint at Exeter, a move seen as risky given the limited resources provided by owner Mike Danson, who is reportedly keen to sell the club. His earlier tenure saw Wigan promoted from the same division in 2015‑16, but the present campaign highlights the challenges of rebuilding under a shoestring budget.
summary: Wigan Athletic are bottom of League One even after a 1-0 victory over Reading on Saturday. Manager Gary Caldwell, the 2013 club captain, returned for a second stint while working under a shoestring budget imposed by owner Mike Danson, who is keen to sell.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig says he never enjoys games ahead of Liverpool match
content: It will be a tense time for Europe’s longest serving president, despite the Champions League game at Anfield offering a symbol of how far they have come The first time Fernando Roig watched Villarreal play as their president, he sat in the stand at a tiny whitewashed ground that had concrete fever and was half empty. It was a Sunday night in the second division, they lost 3-0 against Badajoz, and he didn’t enjoy it much. But then, he never enjoys it much. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous,” he says. “It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious. I suffer a lot.
summary: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig, Europe’s longest‑serving club president, says he never enjoys watching his team play. He said he feels anxious ahead of the Champions League match at Anfield against Liverpool, recalling his first game as president was a 3‑0 loss to Badajoz in the second division.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Three Premier League clubs struggling domestically meet in lesser European competition
content: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.”
summary: Four Premier League clubs are playing each other on Sunday in the lesser continental competitions, with three of them also struggling in their domestic league. In Leiria, fans obtained tickets by emailing the president of Torreense, could sit anywhere in a large stadium, and enjoyed free beer provided by a local patisserie.
author: Guardian Sport

title: New Zealand Silver Ferns beat Australia 56-50 to open Constellation Cup
content: Silver Ferns win 56-50 to open Constellation Cup series Grace Nweke 40 from 41 against world No 1 Diamonds New Zealand signalled their intent to set a new netball world order after stunning the Diamonds to kick off the Constellation Cup. The Commonwealth Games gold medallists picked up in Auckland where they left off in Glasgow with a 56-50 series-opening win at Spark Arena on Sunday. Experienced Diamonds duo Jo Weston (managed) and Kate Moloney (finger) were sorely missed by the world No 1 outfit, who were left in tears in Glasgow after settling for a bronze medal. Australia had suffered a shock semi-final defeat to Jamaica to miss a gold medal match for the first time since the sport joined the Games program in 1998.
summary: The New Zealand Silver Ferns defeated the Australian Diamonds 56-50 at Spark Arena to open the Constellation Cup series. Australia were missing Jo Weston and Kate Moloney and had recently lost a Commonwealth Games semi‑final to Jamaica.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Emma Finucane takes bronze in women's keirin at UCI World Track Championships
content: Great Britain's Emma Finucane is beaten on the line and has to settle for bronze in the women's keirin on the final day the UCI World Track Championships in China.
summary: Great Britain's Emma Finucane was beaten on the line in the women's keirin. She settled for the bronze medal on the final day of the UCI World Track Championships in China.

title: Lara Gillespie wins second straight world title in points race at UCI Track Championships
content: Ireland's Lara Gillespie is world champion for the second season in a row after dominating the points race on the final day of competition at the UCI World Track Championships in China.
summary: Lara Gillespie of Ireland became world champion for a second consecutive season. She secured the title by dominating the points race on the final day of the UCI World Track Championships in China.

title: Pedro Neto scores twice as Chelsea beat Everton 2-0
content:
Pedro Neto scored twice as Chelsea secured a 2-0 victory over Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.  

The win was largely eclipsed by a nasty head injury suffered by Everton goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez during the match.
summary: Pedro Neto scored twice for Chelsea as they defeated Everton 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. The game was overshadowed by a nasty head injury to Emiliano Martinez.

title: Rep. Scott Perry trails Democratic challenger Janelle Stelson by three points in PA poll
content:
A new Susquehanna Polling and Research survey released Saturday shows incumbent Republican Rep. Scott Perry trailing Democratic challenger former news anchor Janelle Stelson in Pennsylvania's key battleground district.  

The poll reports Perry at 46 percent and Stelson at 49 percent, a three‑point gap that falls within the margin of error.
summary: A new Susquehanna Polling and Research survey of a Pennsylvania battleground district shows incumbent Rep. Scott Perry (R) trailing his Democratic opponent. The poll lists Perry at 46 % and former news anchor Janelle Stelson (D) at 49 %, a three‑point lead within the margin of error.

title: Trump issues executive order halting Russia sanctions, sparking bipartisan backlash
content: The Sunday preview highlighted an escalating feud between President Trump and President Zelensky and noted a wave of controversies confronting the White House ahead of the midterm elections. On Friday evening Trump issued an executive order that halted the rollout of new penalties on Russia set to take effect under a sweeping legislative package he signed last month, prompting bipartisan backlash over the administration’s recent easing of Russian sanctions.
summary: President Trump issued an executive order on Friday evening that stopped the implementation of new penalties on Russia set to take effect under a legislative package he signed into law last month. The order provoked bipartisan backlash and comes as the Trump‑Zelensky feud escalates and other controversies hit the White House before the midterms.

title: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemns attack on Washington Post photojournalist
content: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee denounced a “vicious” and “cowardly” assault on a Washington Post photojournalist in the West Bank, urging a full investigation. In a statement posted to X, Huckabee said the attack involved a group of Israeli settlers targeting Palestinians and the journalist.
summary: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemns attack on Washington Post photojournalist.

title: Sen. Darline Graham says she will keep pressure on Russia after Trump waives sanctions
content:
Sen. Darline Graham (R‑S. C.) said Saturday she prefers to maintain sanctions pressure on Russia after President Trump signed an executive order Friday waiving sanctions on Russian energy.  

The waived measures originated from the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a bill Graham previously championed.
summary: Sen. Darline Graham says she will keep pressure on Russia after Trump waives sanctions.
author: The Hill

title: CDC deploys disease expert to Pennsylvania for measles outbreak response
content:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is dispatching a disease expert to Pennsylvania as the state confronts an ongoing measles outbreak.  

A CDC spokesperson told NBC News the agency will keep working closely with Pennsylvania health officials, offering the expertise and support needed to respond to the outbreak and protect public health.
summary: The CDC is sending a disease expert to assist with the response to the ongoing measles outbreak in Pennsylvania. A CDC spokesperson said the agency will continue working closely with Pennsylvania health officials to provide expertise and support to protect public health.

title: New federal rule makes flight compensation harder
content: A new federal rule is set to take effect, meaning passengers whose flights are delayed or canceled may find it harder to obtain compensation. The change applies to all airline travelers affected by cancellations or delays, altering the process for receiving monetary relief.
summary: A new federal rule is set to take effect. It could make it harder to obtain compensation for delayed or canceled flights.

title: Call for research, safeguards and guidance to protect children from AI
content: The article asserts that children will inevitably grow up with artificial intelligence and calls for the development of research, safeguards and scientific guidance to understand AI’s effects on them, urging action while the opportunity still exists to shape future outcomes.
summary: The piece says children will grow up with artificial intelligence. It urges building research, safeguards and scientific guidance to understand AI’s impact on children while there is still an opportunity to shape the future.

title: President Zelensky meets UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham at Downing Street
content: Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday. The Ukrainian leader’s visit comes as he looks to shore up his European allies five years into Russia’s war on Ukraine.
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday. Zelensky is looking to shore up his European allies five years into Russia's war on Ukraine.

title: Reform UK says no room for racism after ITV airs councillors' racist remarks
content: Reform UK faces criticism after ITV News aired undercover footage recorded over a year that captured some of its councillors and candidates using racist, violent and sexist language. The party responded that there is no room for racism within Reform UK.
summary: Reform UK said there is no room for racism in its party. The comment followed ITV News broadcasting undercover footage, collected over a year, of some Reform UK councillors and candidates using racist, violent and sexist language.
author: BBC Politics

title: Iguazu Falls reaches record flow ten times normal, prompting temporary closure
content:
Iguazu Falls, a UNESCO World Heritage site in South America, has recorded a water flow ten times its normal rate after heavy rains across the river basin. El Niño weather patterns are said to have driven the surge, with the usual flow of 1.5 million litres per second rising to 15 million litres per second, according to the local government.

In response to the El Niño‑fuelled increase in water levels, Argentina has temporarily closed Iguazu Falls. The unprecedented flow underscores the impact of the current weather conditions on the iconic waterfall.
summary: Iguazu Falls, a UNESCO world heritage site, recorded a water flow of 15 million litres per second—about ten times its normal 1.5 million litres per second—after heavy rains and El Niño conditions. Argentina temporarily closed the falls due to the surge in water levels.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Insider claims insurers cut loss forecasts to lower prices despite rising climate risk
content: Insurers are taking on more risk than they should. If – or when – a major disaster hits, the catastrophe will have far-reaching consequences I work for a major insurer, assessing the risk posed by natural disasters on properties around the world, from family homes to schools, government offices and multibillion-dollar commercial centres. The world is facing greater risk than ever from extreme weather. We are not prepared – and that inaction could have profound consequences for the global financial system. In the face of ever more extreme and unpredictable climate risks, I am coming under pressure to cut my forecasts for the losses that disasters will cause in order to make insurance more affordable – and get my employer more business. In some instances, the questioning of our numbers and models is justified. But too often, it is not being done to produce more accurate models, but to artificially lower prices. If this is happening at my firm, which is struggling to compete with rivals’ prices, it’s happening elsewhere. The writer is a modeller working in the insurance industry. A version of this piece originally appeared with the Bureau of Investigative Journalism as part of their Secret Source series, a regular column featuring industry whistleblowers
summary: An anonymous insurance modeller says insurers are taking on more risk than they should and are being pressured to cut loss forecasts for natural disasters. He alleges the lowered forecasts are often used to artificially reduce prices and win business, and the piece was first published in the Bureau of Investigative Journalism’s Secret Source series.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Coalition says emissions from Australian fossil fuels burned abroad should be ignored
content: The emissions might occur elsewhere, but they generate global harm that scientists can now quantify Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here The Coalition has come up with the perfect solution to deal with the climate pollution from when Australian fossil fuels are burned overseas. We should either just pretend they don’t exist, or ignore the reason why people are concerned about them, even if those people include a majority of high court judges or the international court of justice. Sign up to get climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s Clear Air column as a free newsletter
summary: The Coalition proposes treating emissions from Australian fossil fuels burned overseas as non‑existent. Those emissions have drawn concern from a majority of high court judges and the International Court of Justice.

title: Reform UK councillor scraps King's Lynn climate emergency declaration after heated vote
content:
The debate over climate‑emergency declarations resurfaced in King’s Lynn and West Norfolk after the council, which had first declared a climate emergency in 2021 while under Conservative control, changed hands to independents and a Reform UK councillor. Reform UK councillor Austen Moore moved to overturn the declaration; the meeting was postponed because extreme heat made the council chamber unusable, and the motion was subsequently rescheduled and defeated by a vote of 33 to seven.

A liveblog by a local scientist and Extinction Rebellion member recorded the proceedings, adding maps that showed most of the county, including King’s Lynn, already lies below the annual flood level. The article notes that similar debates have occurred in other Reform‑led councils, where Reform’s arguments have prevailed. In Kent, councillor Linden Kemkaran argued that climate change is acceptable because the world was warmer in Roman times and that carbon dioxide is a trace gas essential for life, suggesting that cutting emissions would be dangerous.

The piece concludes by promoting the Guardian’s Climate Forum 2026, scheduled for 20 October, featuring Zoe Williams alongside a panel that includes professor Andrew Haines, MP Katie White, Asad Rehman, Shruti Suresh, Gareth Thomas and Amy Fairman. The forum is billed as a hopeful, solutions‑focused evening.
summary: The King's Lynn and West Norfolk council, now controlled by independents and Reform UK councillor Austen Moore, voted 33‑to‑7 to scrap its 2021 climate‑emergency declaration. The motion was delayed because extreme heat forced the council chamber to close, and the vote took place the following week.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Protected sand tiger sharks sold abroad via Delaware Bay loophole
content:
A loophole in U.S. fisheries regulations is allowing private companies to capture protected sand‑tiger sharks and sell them to overseas aquariums, critics say, even as the species benefits from conservation gains in Delaware Bay. While state anglers are barred from taking the endangered fish, the exemption permits commercial firms to harvest the sharks for export, prompting concerns that the Bay’s recent recovery is being monetised.

At about 12:45 p.m., researchers from the University of Delaware witnessed the capture of a sand‑tiger shark on a 300‑metre line in the bay’s murky green waters. The 225‑centimetre, 90‑centimetre‑girth shark was hauled aboard a small boat, measured, sexed and sampled for blood and muscle. A tag was then secured beneath its dorsal fin through its thick, sand‑papery skin, enabling future monitoring of the species despite its removal from the wild.
summary: A loophole permits private firms to catch protected sand tiger sharks in Delaware Bay for export to foreign aquariums, despite bans on anglers taking the endangered species. University of Delaware researchers recently captured, measured, sampled and tagged a 225 cm sand tiger shark in the bay.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Gabon battles US drug firms to protect iboga, a sacred plant eyed for addiction treatment
content:
Gabon is fighting US drug companies to safeguard iboga, a sacred plant that some compare to ayahuasca.  

The bitter root bark, known as iboga, is central to several Gabonese ritual traditions and is believed to have huge potential for treating addiction and some mental illnesses. In a dark temple with a sandy floor edged with candles, participants sit shoulder to shoulder beneath palm fronds and swallow the bark throughout the night.  

Iboga comes from Tabernanthe iboga, a slow‑growing central African rainforest shrub whose root bark has long been used in Gabonese rituals.
summary: Gabon is fighting to protect the iboga root, a sacred plant used in several Gabonese ritual traditions, from US drug companies. The plant’s bark is believed to have huge potential for treating addiction and some mental illnesses.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Miami’s Spice N Curry owner says $370K pandemic loan became a disaster
content: Low-interest loans kept many eateries afloat. But the industry never recovered enough for them to repay the debt For almost 20 years, Jai Mazumdar has served vegetarian curries, samosas, gulab jamun and other Indian delicacies at Spice N Curry, a cafe and grocery nestled inside a modest strip mall near Florida International University (FIU) in Miami. When the Covid-19 pandemic devastated his business, as it did with so many restaurants, Mazumdar took out a $370,000 economic injury disaster loan (EIDL) from the federal government in early 2021. At the time, it provided a desperately needed lifeline. He was confident that once business returned to normal he could begin repaying the 30-year loan, which came with a low 3.75% interest rate and a 30-month deferment period. But when his business didn’t recover, the disaster loan turned out to be a disaster of its own.
summary: Jai Mazumdar, owner of Spice N Curry near Florida International University, took a $370,000 Economic Injury Disaster Loan in early 2021. The restaurant’s post‑pandemic recovery fell short, turning the low‑interest loan into a financial burden.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Salk Institute maps exercise's molecular effects across mouse organs, cells, sexes
content: Salk Institute researchers are creating a scientific reference for bodily health by mapping how exercise reshapes the body at the molecular level. Their latest effort examines exercise‑induced responses across multiple organs, cell types, sexes and circadian phases in mice, aiming to define what a healthy body looks like before studying disease.
summary: Salk Institute researchers are creating a scientific reference for what makes a body healthy. Their latest study maps how exercise reshapes the body at the molecular level, examining responses across organs, cell types, sexes and circadian phases in mice.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Body data may give 24‑hour warning for post‑concussion headaches
content: Researchers have found that the headaches and fatigue many concussion sufferers experience follow a consistent pattern that could be used to warn patients a full day before the symptoms set in. The observation suggests that monitoring body data may provide a 24‑hour advance alert for these post‑concussion effects.
summary: Body data may give 24‑hour warning for post‑concussion headaches.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Lab-designed synthetic peptide reduces amyloid beta in mice
content: A research team led by the Molecular and Cellular Neurobiotechnology group at the Institute for Bioengineering of Catalonia (IBEC) has identified a synthetic peptide that lowers the production of amyloid beta (Aβ), the protein linked to Alzheimer’s disease, in mice. The work was carried out in collaboration with Míriam Royo’s laboratory at the Institute for Advanced Chemistry of Catalonia (IQAC‑CSIC), the University of Barcelona and the Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB Barcelona). The discovery marks a laboratory‑designed molecule capable of reducing amyloid beta levels in an animal model.
summary: Lab-designed synthetic peptide reduces amyloid beta in mice.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Research finds family of critically ill cancer patients face anxiety and depression
content: When cancer patients reach intensive care, doctors concentrate on saving lives, yet research shows that family members, partners and friends bear a heavy burden. The study finds widespread anxiety, depression, exhaustion and declining well‑being among those supporting a loved one through a critical illness.
summary: Doctors are working to save the lives of cancer patients in intensive care. Research shows family members, partners and friends of these patients experience widespread anxiety, depression, exhaustion and declining well‑being.
author: Medical Xpress

title: First responders' brain injury care guidelines released with 28 recommendations
content:
Over 50 experts—clinicians, researchers, policymakers, first responders and representatives from agencies that employ and advocate for them—have reached consensus on the first recommendations for the recognition, diagnosis and management of traumatic brain injury in first responders.  

Publishing today (Oct. 16, 2026) in The Journal of Head Trauma Rehabilitation, the 52 authors agreed to 28 recommendations designed to help first responders, health‑care professionals and agencies work toward five primary goals: timely recognition of traumatic brain injury (TBI), safe recovery, operational readiness, reduced stigma and first‑responder–centered care.
summary: Over 50 experts—clinicians, researchers, policymakers, first responders and representatives from agencies that employ and advocate for them—have reached consensus on the first recommendations for the recognition, diagnosis and management of traumatic brain injury in first responders. title: Limited‑English new moms less likely to receive standard headache treatment after epidural
content:
A study presented at the Anesthesiology 2026 annual meeting found that new mothers with limited English proficiency are less likely to receive the standard treatment for post‑epidural headaches.  

These headaches are painful and debilitating and can occur when the membrane surrounding the spinal cord is accidentally punctured during an epidural for childbirth.
summary: New mothers with limited English proficiency are less likely to receive the standard treatment for painful and debilitating headaches that can occur if the membrane surrounding the spinal cord is accidentally punctured during an epidural for childbirth. The finding was reported in a study presented at the Anesthesiology 2026 annual meeting.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Martin explains consumer rights and cancellation options for auto‑renew subscriptions
content: Martin offered listeners guidance on dealing with auto‑renewing subscriptions, outlining the consumer rights that apply and describing how a renewal can be challenged or cancelled. His advice aims to help those who feel caught out by recurring charges.
summary: Martin provides advice for listeners caught out by auto‑renewing subscriptions. He explains the rights consumers have and whether there is a way to challenge the renewal or cancel.
author: BBC Business

title: Climate change costs remain ambiguous as impacts on extreme weather are hard to measure
content: Human activity has raised global temperatures, but quantifying the direct costs of climate change remains difficult. The impact on extreme weather—such as hurricanes and heat waves—varies locally, and both observations and climate models may fail to capture these effects accurately.
summary: Human activity has raised global temperatures, making it difficult to determine the direct costs of climate change. Impacts on extreme weather such as hurricanes and heat waves are locally specific and variable, and observations and climate models may not fully capture them.
author: Phys.org

title: Australian scavengers approach carcasses like a buffet, not just eat and leave
content:
Scientists often picture scavengers as animals that sniff out a carcass, eat rapidly and then slink away.  

Observations of Australian scavengers contradict that image; they are reported to treat a carcass more like a buffet rather than a quick meal.
summary: Australian scavengers do not simply eat everything and slink away from a carcass. Instead, they approach a carcass as if it were a buffet.
author: Phys.org

title: Salt crystals from Enceladus jets may reveal clues to subsurface ocean life
content: Salt crystals ejected from Saturn’s moon Enceladus may contain evidence of life in its subsurface ocean. Jets near the moon’s south pole spew water vapor and icy particles from the ocean beneath kilometers of ice, allowing scientists to study the hidden water without drilling.
summary: Salt crystals from Enceladus's south‑pole jets could provide clues to possible life in its hidden ocean. The ocean lies beneath kilometers of ice, but water vapor and icy particles ejected by the jets reach the surface, allowing study without drilling.
author: Phys.org

title: Hand‑cranked device determines blood type and hematocrit in one minute
content:
A newly unveiled hand‑cranked device can determine a patient’s blood type and hematocrit level in just one minute. The rapid test aims to give doctors immediate information needed for safe transfusions and to assess blood loss or anemia when injuries are severe.  

Current hospital equipment for these measurements relies on large, electricity‑powered machines and trained personnel, resources that are often missing from ambulances, disaster zones and remote clinics. The portable, manual system could fill that gap by providing critical data without power or specialist staff.
summary: The device can identify a patient’s blood type and red‑cell level within about a minute. It offers a portable alternative to large electric machines that require trained staff, which are often lacking in ambulances, disaster zones or remote clinics.
author: Phys.org

title: Quantum magic state cleanup reduces errors 40‑fold in first hardware test
content: A hardware test of a new quantum “magic state cleanup” technique cut qubit errors by a factor of 40, marking the first successful demonstration of the method. The result addresses the fragility of qubits that hampers reliable quantum computing, offering a less resource‑intensive alternative to traditional magic‑state distillation, which filters flaws but demands extensive overhead.
summary: The new quantum magic state cleanup technique cut errors by a factor of 40 in its first successful hardware test. Qubits are fragile and prone to errors, making reliable quantum computers difficult, and traditional magic state distillation filters flaws but is extremely resource‑intensive.
author: Phys.org

title: LLNL builds 3D simulations to test nuclear asteroid deflection
content:
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory researchers are developing three‑dimensional simulations to assess how a nuclear device could deflect or potentially disrupt an asteroid threatening Earth.  

The simulations aim to evaluate mitigation options for planetary defense.
summary: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory researchers are developing three‑dimensional simulations. The simulations examine how a nuclear device could deflect or disrupt an asteroid threatening Earth.
author: Phys.org

title: Lund University study finds complex population impact after Kikai‑Akahoya eruption
content: An international research team headed by Lund University has investigated how the prehistoric Kikai‑Akahoya volcanic eruption impacted population levels in Japan. The study’s findings, published in Science Advances, suggest that the demographic effects were more nuanced than earlier assumptions indicated. The results revise the understanding of this major volcanic disaster’s societal consequences.
summary: An international study led by Lund University examined population levels after the Kikai‑Akahoya volcanic eruption in prehistoric Japan. The researchers say the results show a more complex picture than previously believed, and the paper appears in Science Advances.
author: Phys.org

title: 1960 scientists' prediction of humanity's brink on Nov 13 2026 proves inaccurate
content:
In 1960, scientists warned that runaway population growth would push humanity to the brink of destruction on November 13, 2026, and their mathematical forecasts appeared to track reality for decades.  

Subsequent declines in birth rates and a slowdown in population growth have undermined the doomsday scenario, illustrating how even convincing scientific models can falter when human behavior shifts.
summary: In 1960 scientists predicted that runaway population growth would bring humanity to the brink of destruction on November 13, 2026, and their mathematical forecasts remained surprisingly accurate for decades. Later declines in birth rates and slower population growth caused the prediction to unravel, showing that scientific models can fail when human behavior changes.
author: Science Daily

title: Archaeologists uncover 1,200‑year‑old hairless dog mummies at Wari site in Peru
content:
Archaeologists have uncovered 1,200‑year‑old remains of Peru’s famed hairless dogs at an ancient Wari Empire burial site.  

The find includes remarkably preserved mummies and puppies interred with humans; analysis of their unusual teeth, diets and burial arrangements provides new insight into how ancient Peruvians cared for, bred and sometimes discarded these animals.
summary: Archaeologists have discovered 1,200‑year‑old remains of Peru’s hairless dogs at an ancient Wari Empire burial site. The find includes remarkably preserved mummies and puppies buried alongside humans, and their unusual teeth, diets and burial arrangements reveal clues about how ancient Peruvians cared for, bred and sometimes discarded their dogs.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists discover youth protein that rejuvenates aging brain immune cells in mice
content:
Scientists discovered a youth‑associated protein that protects the brain’s immune cells from age‑related decline.  

Restoring the protein in older mice improved the cells’ ability to clear debris and reduced signs of inflammation, raising hopes for future treatments targeting brain aging and Alzheimer’s disease.
summary: Scientists discovered a youth‑linked protein that protects the brain’s immune cells from age‑related decline. Restoring the protein in older mice improved the cells’ debris‑clearing ability and reduced inflammation, suggesting potential for treatments targeting brain aging and Alzheimer’s disease.
author: Science Daily

title: Two supermassive black holes in galaxy Mrk 501 may merge within 100 years
content:
Astronomers have uncovered compelling evidence that two supermassive black holes are spiraling toward a potentially spectacular collision at the center of galaxy Mrk 501. A previously unseen jet of particles revealed the likely presence of a second black hole, confirming the binary nature of the system.

Observations indicate the pair completes an orbit every 121 days, and, depending on their masses, the two cosmic giants could merge in as little as 100 years.
summary: Astronomers have found evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward a collision at the center of galaxy Mrk 501. A newly detected particle jet suggests a second black hole, with the pair completing a 121‑day orbit and possibly merging in as little as 100 years.
author: Science Daily

title: New drug reverses severe fatty liver disease in animals by repairing gut
content: Scientists have discovered a potential new drug that reverses severe fatty liver disease in animal models by restoring gut health and preventing harmful substances from reaching the liver. The finding may open pathways for treatments of liver disease and other serious conditions such as cardiovascular disease.
summary: Scientists discovered a potential new drug can reverse severe fatty liver disease in animal models by restoring gut health and blocking harmful substances from reaching the liver. The breakthrough could pave the way for new treatments for liver disease and potentially other serious conditions, including cardiovascular disease.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find many sweeteners disrupt gut bacteria, especially with antidepressant
content: Scientists tested 39 sweeteners and found that many common varieties can interfere with gut bacteria. In laboratory experiments, a mixture of one sweetener with a widely prescribed antidepressant markedly reduced beneficial bacteria and overall microbial diversity, prompting new questions about possible impacts on gut health and immunity.
summary: Scientists discovered that many common sweeteners can interfere with gut bacteria, and some combinations with medications produce strong effects. In laboratory experiments, one sweetener mixed with a widely prescribed antidepressant reduced beneficial bacteria and microbial diversity, raising questions about gut health and immunity.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find deep sleep links growth hormone to muscle gain, fat loss, and brain boost
content:
Scientists discovered a two‑way relationship between sleep and growth hormone, showing deep sleep builds muscle, burns fat and boosts brain function.  

The research indicates the brain balances physical recovery with wakefulness, explaining how inadequate sleep harms metabolism and brain health and may pave the way for treatments targeting sleep and neurological disorders.
summary: Scientists discovered a two‑way relationship between sleep and growth hormone that shows the brain balances physical recovery with wakefulness. The findings may explain why poor sleep harms metabolism and brain health and could lead to new treatments for sleep and neurological disorders.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find female mouse skin cells coordinate, male cells act independently
content:
Scientists have uncovered a surprising difference in how male and female skin repairs and renews itself. By tracking individual skin stem cells in living mice for five months, researchers observed distinct patterns of cellular behavior between the sexes.

Female skin stem cells were found to work together in a highly coordinated manner, whereas male cells operated more independently. The synchronization, driven by sex hormones, appears to explain why wounds heal faster in female mice, particularly during the first few days after injury.
summary: Researchers tracked individual skin stem cells in living mice for five months and observed that female cells work together in a highly coordinated way while male cells operate more independently. This hormone-driven synchronization helps explain why wounds heal faster in female mice, especially during the first few days.
author: Science Daily

title: Walmart sells digital Pikmin 4 for $39.88, $20 off, with $10 Switch 2 upgrade
content:
Walmart is offering the digital version of Pikmin 4 for Nintendo Switch at $39.88, more than $20 below its regular $59.99 price, according to a tip from colleague Sheena Vasani. The discount is available for instant digital delivery.

The game continues the series’ puzzle formula while introducing a dog companion that adds extra complexity and action, and it explores darker undertones hinted at in earlier titles.

Nintendo announced that a Switch 2 edition of Pikmin 4 will launch on November 12th, 2026, featuring polished visuals, voice commands for the dog companion, and a new “Dandori Academy” mode with ongoing challenges. Players can upgrade to this edition for $10, a $20 saving compared with purchasing the $69.99 Switch 2 version outright.
summary: Walmart sells digital Pikmin 4 for $39.88, $20 off, with $10 Switch 2 upgrade.

content: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. title: Independent arcades see resurgence as players shift from sprawling “forever games”
content:
A semi‑nostalgic movement is emerging in the gaming world as players turn back to more focused, social experiences, prompting speculation that a new wave of independent arcades could revive the communal side of gaming. The shift follows a five‑year period during which major publishers poured hundreds of millions of dollars into “forever games” such as Fortnite, Minecraft and Roblox, creating sprawling franchises built around endless updates and battle‑pass systems.

Industry observers note that this emphasis on perpetual content has produced notable failures, including titles like Concord, Mindseye and Tales of the Shire. Even well‑received releases such as Crimson Desert, Path of Exile 2 and Blood of the Dawnwalker are described as overly bloated, consuming large portions of players’ limited free time. The growing discontent with these expansive models is fueling interest in smaller, arcade‑style venues that prioritize direct, social play.
summary: After years of sprawling ‘forever’ games, players are rediscovering the pleasures of more focused experiences. Could a new wave of independent arcades bring back the social side of gaming?

title: Apple AirPods 5 reviewed as best open‑fit earbuds with upgraded ANC
content:
Apple has unveiled the AirPods 5, positioning them as the best open‑fit earbuds yet. The new model keeps the familiar design of the popular AirPods 4 but removes silicone ear tips, offering a noise‑cancelling experience that rivals many plugged‑in designs at a lower price.

The AirPods 5 come in two versions—one with a wireless charging case and swipe controls, the other without. Prices start at £119 (€149/$129/A$219), £10 cheaper than the launch price of their predecessors. Connectivity is handled by Bluetooth 5.3, SBC, AAC, and the new H2 chip. Battery life is four to five hours with ANC, extending to 22 hours with the case. The earbuds are water‑resistant (IP57, up to 1 metre for 30 minutes) and weigh 4.3 g each.

The charging case measures 46.2 × 50.1 × 21.2 mm and weighs 32.3 g (wireless) or 34.7 g (wired). It can be charged via USB‑C or wirelessly using Qi or Apple Watch charging standards.
summary: Apple’s AirPods 5 keep the AirPods 4 design but omit silicone tips and add upgraded active‑noise cancelling that rivals many plugged‑in earbuds. They are sold with or without a wireless‑charging case, start at £119 (about $129), and deliver four to five hours of use with ANC and up to 22 hours total from the case.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI Threat: Lack of Public Voice Fuels Resistance Against Tech-White House Alliance
content: The tech bros and their highly paid sock puppets are banking on us giving in to their ‘inevitability doctrine’. But in Australia, and around the world, resistance is rising Of all the drivers of the populist wave, one of the most powerful is the sense of inevitability that surrounds what we are told is the march of progress. In presenting the future as a fait accompli, it poisons the civic well by dealing us out of the game. While the US clings on to its status as the oldest constitutional democracy, the unholy alliance between the tech overlords and the White House is creating its own AI reality untethered to the will of the people.
summary: Tech bros and their paid sock puppets rely on an inevitability doctrine that erodes public agency. In Australia and worldwide, resistance grows as the tech overlords and the White House forge an AI reality detached from the people's will.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta scales back AI-driven staff cuts after workers spent time fixing errors
content:
Rapid AI adoption has left workers cleaning up a flood of errors and low‑quality work, employers around the globe are grappling with the fallout, Reuters reported. Meta has scaled back plans to axe staff and deploy more AI agents after the company discovered employees were spending increasing time fixing technical and security errors.

In a separate move, after thinning its workforce—especially middle managers—in a 2023 efficiency push, Meta is expanding its managerial ranks again, LinkedIn posts from workers show.
summary: Employers worldwide are grappling with fallout from rapid AI adoption that left workers cleaning up technical and security errors. Meta has scaled back plans to axe staff and use more AI agents and is expanding its managerial ranks after a 2023 efficiency-driven workforce reduction, according to Reuters and LinkedIn posts.

title: Morning news bulletin for October 16, 2026 covering Europe and global stories
content:
This morning’s bulletin delivers the most important stories from across Europe and beyond on October 16, 2026.  

It covers a range of topics, including the latest news, breaking news, world events, business, entertainment, politics, culture, and travel.
summary: The October 16, 2026 morning bulletin provides a roundup of key stories from Europe and beyond. It includes the latest news, breaking news, and coverage of world, business, entertainment, politics, culture, and travel.

title: Rubio lands in Samarkand for C5+1 talks with Central Asian foreign ministers
content:
Rubio arrives in Samarkand as Washington seeks closer ties with Central Asia.  

The US secretary of state will meet the foreign ministers of five Central Asian countries on Monday under the C5+1 format.  

Trade, investment, critical minerals and security are expected to feature in discussions, while more than 200 American business executives accompany the visit.
summary: The US secretary of state will meet the foreign ministers of five Central Asian countries on Monday under the C5+1 format. Trade, investment, critical minerals and security are expected to feature in discussions, while more than 200 American business executives accompany the visit.

title: Huge smoke and flames over St Petersburg after large Ukrainian drone attack
content:
Huge plumes of black smoke billowed over St Petersburg, Russia’s second‑largest city, on Sunday, 18 October, as a large‑scale Ukrainian drone attack sparked fires at industrial and logistics facilities.  

Russian officials said 126 drones had been intercepted in the surrounding region.
summary: On Sunday, 18 October, huge plumes of black smoke rose over St Petersburg after a large‑scale Ukrainian drone attack set fire to industrial and logistics facilities. Russian officials said 126 drones were intercepted in the surrounding region.
author: Euronews

title: PSG regain Ligue 1 lead after comeback win over Strasbourg
content:
PSG reclaimed the Ligue 1 lead after a dramatic comeback against Strasbourg, overturning a deficit that had persisted for over 60 minutes. The Parisians relied on their substitutes to secure the turnaround.  

The win follows PSG’s spectacular Champions League triumph over Manchester City and comes as the club prepares to face FC Barcelona, with confidence at an all‑time high.
summary: PSG trailed Strasbourg for more than 60 minutes before substitutes helped them turn the game around. The win puts PSG back on top of Ligue 1 and follows their Champions League victory over Manchester City ahead of a clash with Barcelona.
author: France 24

title: Paris police report record 855 arrests in protest violence, 500+ detained
content: Police in Paris announced on Sunday that they had arrested a record 855 people for protest‑related violence the day before. The prosecutor’s office said more than 500 of those individuals were being held in custody, according to France 24 analyst Shirli Sitbon.
summary: Police in Paris said Sunday they had arrested a "record" 855 people over protest-related violence in the capital the day before. The prosecutor's office said more than 500 of those arrested were being held in custody.
author: France 24

title: Violence erupts at France's Saturday protests, ~400 arrested, TV2 investigates perpetrators
content: Violent clashes, fires, vandalism and looting marred demonstrations across France on Saturday as hundreds of thousands marched against the rising cost of living and poor conditions in schools. The French Interior Ministry said about 400 people were arrested nationwide, and partner TV station France 2 examined who was involved in the violence.
summary: Violent clashes, fires, vandalism and looting marred demonstrations across France on Saturday as hundreds of thousands marched against the rising cost of living and poor school conditions. title: Michael Gove explains his support for austerity on Radical Thinking podcast
content: For more than three decades, Michael Gove has been a leading figure in British Conservatism. As a journalist, government minister and now editor of the Tory bible the Spectator, he has helped shape the right even as it has moved further rightwards. In the latest episode of Radical Thinking, Gove joins Aditya Chakrabortty to discuss the future of the right, his record on Brexit and austerity, and the Spectator’s position on Islam Watch the full episode with Michael Gove here. Aditya’s suggested reading: To read the fruits of Michael Gove’s dalliance with the Marxism Today gang, look up his essay in a 1998 collection called The Moderniser’s Dilemma: Radical Politics in the Age of Blair For a slalom ride through Michael Gove’s years in power, read The Demented Dalek by the historian Richard J Evans in the London Review of Books To learn more on what’s become of the British right, there’s a Guardian column by Aditya Phil Burton-Cartledge analyses in depth why the most successful political party is now failing in his book The Party’s Over: The Rise and Fall of the Conservatives from Thatcher to Sunak Phil also writes a very good blog on British politics, which keeps a close eye on how each party is trying to marshall a coalition of voters. Here he is on Kemi Badenoch Geoffrey Wheatcroft does an entertaining short narrative in Bloody Panico!: or, Whatever Happened to The Tory Party For more on the economics of the Cameron years, this paper is acute on how the Tories failed to move the UK away from being a country of renters towards a country of makers. Two of its authors will join us for a podcast later in the series. And if you want to read how Brexit may have cost the UK 8% of GDP, there’s this paper based on data from the Bank of England Finally, on the Spectator, read Nesrine Malik’s recent Guardian column Why has Britain’s oldest political magazine become such a rabid cheerleader for Islamophobia?
summary: Michael Gove joins Aditya Chakrabortty on the Radical Thinking podcast to discuss the future of the right, his record on Brexit and austerity, and the Spectator’s stance on Islam. content: Pope Leo XIV thanked well‑wishers in his first public appearance since a lung‑cancer diagnosis and surgery, reciting the traditional Angelus prayer from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace. The brief ceremony marked his return to duties following the operation.
