title: Meeting science finds bosses should speak less in meetings
content: Close to 1 billion meetings take place each day around the world. CEOs spend nearly three-quarters of their workdays in meetings. Planning for and spearheading meetings eats up the lion’s share of managers’ time. In much of the industrialized world, meetings are both the metronomes and menaces of people’s working lives. Given the enormous time spent in workplace meetings, do we know what they accomplish or how to make them as worthwhile as possible? For decades, the answer was… not really. Meetings weren’t a particularly accessible subject of study. But that has changed. Once a tiny niche area, “meeting science” is a growing specialization among organizational and social psychologists. The field is accelerating as archived virtual meetings provide vast swaths of data. And it is providing a fascinating window into human behavior. Meeting to talk helps fulfill basic human needs to connect, communicate, and cooperate. People have long come together—in caves, fields, market squares, and town halls—to get something done, share ideas, get on the same page, or just to remark on the weather. But meeting scientists define their subject as gatherings of people “with some goal or structure to the event,” says organizational psychologist Liana Kreamer of the Florida Institute of Technology, who coauthored a review of over three decades of meeting science in the 2026 Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior. Read full article Comments
summary: CEOs spend nearly three-quarters of their workdays in meetings, and meeting science is a growing field studying their effectiveness. Organizational psychologist Liana Kreamer of the Florida Institute of Technology coauthored a review of over three decades of meeting science in the 2026 Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior.

title: Wikipedia's 68 million articles consulted trillions of times despite trust concerns
content: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years ago A few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about. Everyone was on it all the time, and yet its reputation had stalled at “don’t trust it”, because it was the “free encyclopedia that anyone can edit”. Clearly people were trusting it, so much so it had become part of the fabric of everyday life since it was founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001. But despite the fact it now has been consulted trillions of times by billions of people (English Wikipedia alone is 5.2bn words long), it inspires an odd lack of curiosity. Even people donating to Wikipedia might say the money was “for the factcheckers”, though there aren’t any – not paid ones, anyway. Meanwhile, the internet in the social media era had begun to feel like a much uglier place, and some digital nostalgia was setting in: here was this holdover that had somehow survived; a website that functions – and even looks – much the same as it did 20 years ago.
summary: Wikipedia has 68 million articles and has been consulted trillions of times. Founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001, the site’s reputation remains challenged by perceptions that it is untrustworthy.

title: Tech billionaires spend over $1 million daily to oppose California’s Prop 40 billionaire tax
content: Tech billionaires have raised more than $340m to defeat Prop 40, a one-time 5% wealth tax that will fund healthcare and education Tech billionaires have been dumping hundreds of millions of dollars into the fight against a wealth tax in California. They’ve raised more than $340m, and the campaign they’re funding is spending more than $1m a day to defeat the measure, according to state financial disclosures. With the election less than a month away, those funds are being spent at a stepped-up pace. During the first 19 days of September, according to the most recent campaign filings, the opposition campaign plowed through at least $21.2m to fight the billionaire tax – surpassing $1m per day. Voters are being inundated with robotexts, mailers and advertisements that warn a tax on billionaires would “expose all Californians to higher taxes”, as one ad reads.
summary: Tech billionaires spend over $1 million daily to oppose California’s Prop 40 billionaire tax.

title: Oscar‑tipped documentary examines the enduring fascination with Elizabeth Holmes
content: The entrepreneur turned fraudster is the subject of an Oscar-tipped new documentary that takes an unusual look at her strange legacy David Agus’s first encounter with Elizabeth Holmes at a health conference came as a shock. The Holmes he met in the green room was personable and pleasant. The Holmes he interviewed on stage was altogether different. “The accent changed: this deep voice, very serious,” Agus, a medical oncologist, recalls by phone from Los Angeles. “It was as if I had met a person and then interviewed a separate person. That transition from the green room to the stage – I had never experienced something like that before.”
summary: The Oscar‑tipped new documentary examines the strange legacy of entrepreneur‑turned‑fraudster Elizabeth Holmes. Medical oncologist David Agus said his first meeting with Holmes at a health conference was pleasant in the green room, but on stage she spoke with a deep, serious voice and a different accent.

content:

title: Britain urged to reject cheap, open-weight Chinese AI from DeepSeek and Xiaomi
content:
Britain is being urged to turn away from inexpensive Chinese artificial‑intelligence products, which critics say lack the security safeguards and benign intent typically built into Western technology.  

Chinese firms such as DeepSeek and Xiaomi are releasing new “open‑weight” AI models each month, allowing businesses and governments in the West to download and run the core software without paying ongoing licence fees, a practice that has sparked fears about the safety and reliability of the technology.
summary: Chinese AI developers such as DeepSeek and Xiaomi release monthly “open-weight” models that can be used without paying an ongoing licence. The article argues that the lack of security and benign intent in Chinese AI creates a risk for businesses and governments in the west.

title: Austrian Green MEP Lena Schilling urges EU action after nude deepfakes surface
content: Lena Schilling of Austrian Greens says images are ‘digital violence against women’ and a threat to democracy An Austrian MEP has spoken out about her experience of being “stripped naked” online without her consent and has urged the EU to take action, as a report found that one in six female MEPs had been targeted by sexualised AI-generated content. Lena Schilling of the Green party said she had learned last month about nude deepfakes of herself circulating online. When she opened the links, she found herself staring at images from one of her first ever press conferences – but the images had been digitally altered to remove her clothing.
summary: Austrian Green MEP Lena Schilling urges EU action after nude deepfakes surface.

title: Anthropic reports AI worm that self‑replicates across smart TVs
content:
Anthropic’s offensive research team released a report this week describing a self‑replicating “AI worm” that can spread autonomously through internet‑connected smart televisions and potentially other ordinary devices. The red‑team researchers built a malicious AI program that divided itself across 15 televisions, allowing each fragment to draw a small amount of power from its host and collectively maintain functionality.

The team noted that while AI‑driven software typically requires substantial computing resources, the worm’s design shows that capability can be distributed across low‑power devices. Anthropic warned that current trends in hardware and software could make such AI worms feasible by the end of the year, raising concerns about the ease with which future AI malware might propagate without human intervention.
summary: Anthropic reports AI worm that self‑replicates across smart TVs.

title: World Bank urges developing nations to build low‑connectivity “small AI” models
content:

Bank’s chief knowledge officer Paschal Donohoe said the tech could speed up economic development from centuries to decades.  

He noted that while Silicon Valley big tech firms focus on ever more sophisticated consumer products, AI could accelerate development for emerging economies only if it is adapted to local needs.
summary: The World Bank is urging developing countries to create “small AI” models that can run on a mobile phone with low connectivity. Chief knowledge officer Paschal Donohoe said such AI could accelerate economic development for emerging economies if adapted to local needs.

content:

The museum published the images after a US expedition to Nikumaroro sparked renewed interest in the long‑standing mystery, providing amateur sleuths with new material to examine for possible traces of the pioneering aviator and her plane.
summary: Air Force Museum of New Zealand releases 1938 aerial photos of Nikumaroro.

title: Argentina's president targets Falkland oil sector, warns fisheries amid renewed hostility
content: Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn. Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors, of varying popularity, gazed disinterestedly at the scene.
summary: Argentina’s president, whose poll numbers are falling, has begun economic attacks on the Falkland Islands’ oil industry. He has also suggested the islands’ key fisheries sector could be targeted next.

title: Descendant celebrates biography of Sarah Forbes Bonetta, gifted to Queen Victoria
content:

content:

title: Optical imaging links altered metabolism and oxygen use in Alzheimer's disease
content:
Optical imaging techniques have revealed a connection between altered metabolism and oxygen utilization in Alzheimer's disease. While the disorder is widely recognized for impairing memory and cognition, researchers note that it also disrupts how brain cells generate and consume energy.

Mitochondria, the cellular structures that provide most of a cell’s energy, can become dysfunctional in the disease. Concurrently, changes in cerebral blood flow and oxygen availability may increase metabolic demands on brain tissue. Understanding the interaction of these factors could aid scientists in characterizing the metabolic changes that accompany Alzheimer’s disease.
summary: Alzheimer's disease involves changes in brain cell energy production and use, including mitochondrial dysfunction and altered blood flow and oxygen availability. Optical imaging links these altered metabolism and oxygen use, aiding researchers in characterizing disease-related metabolic changes.

title: Brain PET scans aid selection and monitoring of patients for new Alzheimer's drugs
content:
Brain PET scans are increasingly used to select and monitor patients receiving new Alzheimer’s disease therapies, according to recent reports on nuclear medicine advances.  

Amyloid PET imaging is employed to confirm the presence of amyloid pathology, helping clinicians decide whether to prescribe anti‑amyloid drugs. In addition, tau PET scans are used to supply further information on disease progression and prognosis.  

These imaging tools enable clinicians to visualize the biological changes associated with Alzheimer’s disease and guide treatment decisions for patients undergoing novel therapies.
summary: Nuclear medicine, including brain PET scans, is increasingly used to visualize biological changes in Alzheimer's disease and guide treatment decisions. Amyloid PET imaging confirms amyloid pathology for patients on anti‑amyloid drugs, and tau PET scans add information on disease progression and prognosis.

title: Study: Justifying political violence increases voter approval, among BJP supporters
content:

The research was conducted by Ursula Daxecker, director at the Max Planck Institute for Politics and Social Science in Göttingen, and Neeraj Prasad of the University of Amsterdam.

The authors find that presenting violence as legitimate increases public approval not only of the violent acts themselves but also of the political parties that employ them. The effect is especially pronounced among supporters of India’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), who, when exposed to justifications for violence, show reduced approval of a peaceful response offered by their own party.

title: Apple Updates App Store Rules to Ban ‘Nudify’ AI Apps
content:
Apple has revised its App Store rules to explicitly ban “nudify” apps that use artificial‑intelligence tools to generate intimate images of people without their consent.  

The rule changes follow criticism after X users employed the AI program Grok earlier this year to create nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes, some involving minors. Apple has not removed X or Grok from the App Store, but it told senators that it threatened to pull Grok.  

At Apple’s WWDC event in June, protestors urged the company to remove Grok, X, and all nudify technology from the App Store. In July, a San Francisco city attorney ordered Apple to delete 13 nudify apps.  

The full story was reported by The Verge.
summary: Apple's App Store rules now explicitly ban "nudify" apps that generate intimate images without consent using AI tools. The changes follow criticism after X users used Grok to create nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes, including minors, and a San Francisco city attorney ordered Apple to remove 13 nudify apps.

title: Apple unveils iPhone Duo foldable phone with 5.4‑inch outer and 7.6‑inch inner displays
content:
Apple has announced its long‑rumored foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo. The new device features a 5.4‑inch outer display and a 7.6‑inch inner display with a “nano‑texture” finish and almost no visible crease. Instead of Face ID, the phone uses Touch ID on the power button and is equipped with a main lens and a wide‑angle lens.

Apple has also redesigned iOS 27 for the foldable, moving the dock to the side of the phone and adding a flashy opening animation when the device is unfolded. The iPhone Duo is Apple’s first foldable and is positioned as a high‑end offering, with the base 256 GB model starting at $1,999 and higher models priced above that.

Preorder demand for the iPhone Duo has been described by Apple as “extraordinary,” but orders are already delayed into 2027. The phone is available for preorder at $1,999, with preorders opening tomorrow.
summary: Apple unveils iPhone Duo foldable phone with 5.4‑inch outer and 7.6‑inch inner displays.

content:

content:
